_doc: Point-in-time retrospective. Every input was public on as_of; see sources. Hindsight lives only in outcome.json.
methodology: house v2 (EPP-distance adjustment), 6-section format; retro method r2: scenario inputs derived from dated facts by frozen rules (retro/README.md); railroad signals

pit_profile.why: Union Pacific: the largest railroad in North America, covering 23 states across the western two-thirds of the US, with BNSF its main rail competitor on parallel routes; carload volume follows the industrial economy, the franchise does not

classification.quality_note: Union Pacific: the largest railroad in North America, covering 23 states across the western two-thirds of the US, with BNSF its main rail competitor on parallel routes; carload volume follows the industrial economy, the franchise does not. durable franchise (obsolescence risk 2/5); price rich; Ratio B 5.55x; +90% to EPP floor; model-vs-market gap +0.25; conservative 2yr -10%.

BEAR.desc: EPS -29.0%/yr (worst year FY00-FY09, capped at 0%); P/E to its 10th pct

BASE.desc: EPS +21.7%/yr (Q3 2010 revenue + margin + buyback); P/E at its 10-yr median

BULL.desc: EPS +21.7%/yr (FY00-FY09 CAGR); P/E holds its 75th pct

XBULL.desc: EPS +42.6%/yr (best 2-yr run FY00-FY09); P/E at its 90th pct

summary: UNP (retrospective, 2010-12-10) ✕ AVOID — Ratio B 5.55x (74.1% downside to Bear $24 / +13.3% upside to Bull $105) | Adj composite 3.50 vs market 3.25: gap +0.25 [MODESTLY UNDERVALUED] | +91% above the EPP floor $49 (13x FY10E $3.74) | Conservative 2-yr case: -9.8% total (-4.9%/yr) | At 24.8x FY10E the 15% hurdle price $123 sits above the BULL case; carloads +14% in Q3 2010, forward revenue +21% (no FY10 revenue guide, Q3 2010 freight revenue); no disruption theme has dated evidence.

sources.title: Union Pacific Corporation 8-K: FY2009 10-K sections as adjusted for the change in accounting for rail grinding
sources.supports: selected financial data 2005-2009 as adjusted (diluted EPS 2005 $1.90, 2006 $2.94, 2007 $3.44, 2008 $4.53, 2009 $3.74; 2009 operating ratio 76.1%); 2009 effective tax rate 36.4%; rail grinding costs expensed as incurred from 2010-01-01, prior periods adjusted

sources.title: Union Pacific Corporation FY2009 10-K
sources.supports: selected financial data 2005-2009 (diluted EPS 2009 $3.75, operating ratio 76.0%); 2009 effective tax rate 36.5%, interest expense $600M, other income $195M, free cash flow $515M; no shares repurchased under the program in 2009; 2010 Outlook in words only (volume to increase from 2009 levels); capital investments of about $2.5 billion

sources.title: Union Pacific Corporation FY2004 10-K
sources.supports: ten-year selected financial data 1995-2004 on the continuing-operations basis (trucking reclassified as discontinued): 1998 loss from continuing operations ($0.41 per diluted share), 1999 $3.05, 2000 $3.22 (includes a $72M after-tax work force reduction charge); operating revenue 1999 $10,175M, 2000 $10,765M

sources.title: Union Pacific Corporation FY2005 10-K
sources.supports: selected financial data 2001-2005: 2001 diluted EPS from continuing operations $3.65, operating revenues $10,830M

sources.title: Union Pacific Corporation Q4 2005 results (8-K ex.99.1)
sources.supports: company-published EPS excluding one-offs: 2004 $2.89 per diluted share excluding the non-cash asbestos charge ($2.30 reported), 2005 $3.41 excluding the income tax expense reduction ($3.85 reported)

sources.title: Union Pacific Corporation FY2006 10-K
sources.supports: selected financial data 2002-2006 (operating revenue, diluted EPS from continuing operations, operating margin and ratio, carloads); 2006 diluted shares 272.0M, effective tax rate 36.4%, interest expense $477M, other income $118M; competition (BNSF parallel routes); 2007 Outlook: commodity revenue growth target 6% to 7%, volume growth 2% to 3%, earnings growth of 10% to 15% and an operating ratio below 80%; quarterly dividend raised to $0.35 on 2007-01-30; 20M-share repurchase authorized 2007-01-30 through 2009

sources.title: Union Pacific Corporation FY2007 10-K
sources.supports: selected financial data 2003-2007; 2007 diluted shares 268.4M, effective tax rate 38.4%, interest expense $482M, other income $116M; 2008 Outlook: earnings of $7.75 to $8.25 per diluted share, volume within a range of 1% higher to 1% lower than 2007, fuel prices 15% to 20% above the 2007 average, record revenue and an improved operating ratio in words; capital investments of about $3.1 billion

sources.title: Union Pacific Corporation FY2002 10-K
sources.supports: 2000 weighted-average diluted shares 269.5M (earnings per share note)

sources.title: Union Pacific Corporation Q4 2009 results (8-K ex.99.1)
sources.supports: Q4 and full-year 2009 freight revenue statistics by business group (revenue, carloads, average revenue per car), operating ratio, GTMs per employee, diluted EPS ($3.75 for 2009) and shares, effective tax rate, interest expense and other income, cash, free cash flow; 2010 outlook in words only

sources.title: Union Pacific Corporation Q1 2010 results (8-K ex.99.1)
sources.supports: Q1 2010 freight revenue statistics by business group, operating ratio, GTMs per employee, diluted EPS (includes a $45M one-time payment to CSXI) and shares, cash; prior-year figures adjusted for the rail grinding accounting change; outlook in words only

sources.title: Union Pacific Corporation Q2 2010 results (8-K ex.99.1)
sources.supports: Q2 2010 freight revenue statistics by business group, operating ratio, GTMs per employee, diluted EPS and shares, cash, share repurchases (nearly 6.5 million); outlook in words only

sources.title: Union Pacific Corporation Q3 2010 results (8-K ex.99.1)
sources.supports: Q3 2010 freight revenue statistics by business group, operating ratio, GTMs per employee, diluted EPS and shares, cash, share repurchases (more than 7.6 million); outlook in words only

sources.title: Union Pacific Corporation 8-K: quarterly dividend raised to 38 cents
sources.supports: quarterly dividend increased by 5 cents to 38 cents per share

sources.title: Union Pacific Corporation 8-K ex.99.1: 2-for-1 stock split, additional share repurchase authorization and second quarter dividend
sources.supports: two-for-one stock split distributed as a stock dividend; repurchase of a further 20 million shares (40 million post-split) by March 2011; quarterly dividend of 44 cents (22 cents post-split)
